html:
SMTO-LLM-0018 — The model got stuck repeating itself

GUID: 446d7328-2dde-4562-ba4b-63d54b52156f
Slug: model-generation-repetitive
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model kept repeating the same thinking, or the same data in an action it was writing, instead of finishing. SMTO stopped that reply before acting on it, so nothing from it was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you asked for a file or data that really has many identical lines, open Settings › Setup › Model routing, expand Tool-call repetition, and raise Minimum repetitions or Minimum repeated characters. Large, intentionally repetitive data can look like a loop, and these changes apply from the model's next reply, even in this task.
  2. On the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). SMTO did not act on the stopped reply, so trying the step again is safe and earlier finished steps are kept.
  3. If it repeats again, turn Thinking off below the message box (select Controls if hidden) and ask SMTO to continue in a new message. Repetition can also start in the model's hidden thinking, and turning thinking off removes that part for new messages.

What success looks like

  • The model finishes the step and the task moves on without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model; the model or its server settings may need adjusting. Don't turn off Stop extreme tool-call repetition unless the repeated data is really what you want.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The generation progress guard confirmed sustained repetition in the model's private reasoning, or extreme repetition in unfinished tool-call arguments, and stopped the response before execution (model_generation_repetitive).

What this means

  • A bounded request-local detector confirmed sustained repetition in private reasoning or extreme repetition in unfinished tool-call arguments. By default, tool arguments require at least eight copies spanning 16,384 characters, confirmed across two checks. The tool-call switch and both thresholds are configurable in Settings > Setup > Model routing > Tool-call repetition and apply at the next model call. This can also interrupt intentionally large repetitive tool data. Answer prose and smaller tool-data repetitions remain diagnostic-only. Similar ideas and revisited conclusions are not sufficient evidence. No incomplete operation was executed.

Why this can happen

  • The active generation-quality check detected excessive repeated fragments.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the retained repetition counters and model configuration with a small test. If the behavior repeats, ask the provider operator to inspect the model and generation settings.

How to fix it

  • Inspect repeated_fragment_count, repeated_period_characters, repeated_window_characters and tool_argument_repetition in provider_diagnostic. For intentionally repetitive tool data, raise llm_tool_argument_repetition_min_repeats or llm_tool_argument_repetition_min_chars (Settings › Setup › Model routing › Tool-call repetition; applies at the next model call); for unintended loops, have the provider operator adjust sampling or thinking settings. Do not replay completed tools.
  • Inspect the repetition counters and model output. For intentionally repetitive tool data, adjust Tool-call repetition in Settings > Setup > Model routing; changes apply at the next model call. Ask the provider operator to investigate unintended loops. Keep previous valid work and do not replay completed tools.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A controlled response makes progress and finishes without crossing the repetition guard.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The current decision is rejected before tool authorization when enforcement applies; earlier results are not replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
